Bayer Annual Report 2025, note [4] table B 4/2 'Key data by segment': Pharmaceuticals, and the segment key data tables in Bayer Annual Report 2025 (A 2.2.2/1, /4 and /7): EBITDA before special items of EUR 4,525mm, less restructuring of 248mm (a recurring cost, so kept in), less cash flow-relevant capital expenditures of 870mm, is 3,407mm. Bayer's unallocated costs are then shared by sales: All Other Segments' EBITDA before special items of 277mm, Enabling Functions and Consolidation's -662mm, 45mm of restructuring in the Reconciliation and the 426mm of group capital expenditure the three segments do not report, -856mm in all, of which 39.40% (-337mm) is this segment's share of the 45,253mm the three segments sell. The three lines above leave 3,790mm, so the charge takes 720mm, 4.0398% of sales, and the segment keeps 3,070mm. Before interest: the target is struck above the financial result. Checked at replacement capex: Bayer does not split plant depreciation from amortisation by segment, so the charge carries the capital expenditure each segment reports in cash. Without one-off cash: litigation special items (group EUR 7,455mm in 2025) are left out and the provisions they built are carried as claims on equity instead; divestment gains are left out. Restated without working capital build: EBITDA is struck before working capital, so the build is charged on growth by the book instead. Across the three segments the targets sum to 6,587mm, which is the group's EBITDA before special items of 9,669mm less 595mm of restructuring and 2,487mm of capital expenditures

column11: already approved in this population, so the layer adds nothing. The Hyrnuo label (DailyMed set id d7a11334-6e7a-445b-9a16-bdcd9acbe61f, spl version 10, effective 2026-09-23, the row the book's labels table carries and the current version on DailyMed's own history endpoint) states that 'HYRNUO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) activating mutations, as detected by an FDA-authorized test', with no restriction on prior therapy. SOHO-02 (NCT06452277) enrols that same labelled population untreated: 'Documented histologically or cytologically confirmed locally advanced non-squamous NSCLC ... or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC', 'Documented activating HER2 mutation in the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD)' and 'No prior systemic therapy for locally advanced or metastatic disease'. Section 14.1 of the same label shows the accelerated approval already rested in part on untreated patients: 'The efficacy population included treatment naive patients (Group F, N=69)'. The book's Enhertu row for this same indication carries 1.0 for the identical situation
column12: the readout moves share of line and evidence, not patients. A SOHO-02 win would put sevabertinib ahead of platinum chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab in first line and convert the accelerated approval, which is a real commercial gain; on this book's convention that a line of therapy is sold to the year's diagnoses, the first-line and later-line patients are the same 192,650 NSCLC diagnoses, so a bottom-up layer would buy them twice. The place for the gain is the marketed line's growth rate. No pool, eligibility, penetration or ramp row is written: indication_layer.build returns early on an overlap of 1.0 and asks for none
